newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says China pressured U.N. chief on S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says China pressured U.N. chief on S.Africa.

text.p: A Taipei diplomat has alleged that rival China used U.N. chief Boutros Boutros-Ghali's re-election hopes to pressure South Africa into abandoning its diplomatic support for Taiwan.

Loh I-cheng, freshly recalled as ambassador to South Africa to protest Pretoria's plan to switch its ties to Beijing, said he learned from South African President Nelson Mandela that Boutros-Ghali had been pressuring Pretoria on Beijing's behalf.

Loh, in interviews with Taiwan media published on Wednesday, said Boutros-Ghali agreed to pressure Mandela as a condition for receiving Beijing's support for his own ill-fated bid to remain U.N. secretary general for a second term.

"When Boutros-Ghali visited South Africa in April he forcefully urged Mandela to establish ties with communist China because he wanted communist China to support his bid for re-election," the United Daily News quoted Loh as saying.
"This is a fact known by all," Loh said.

In the end, China's support for Boutros-Ghali was not enough to overcome opposition to his re-election by the United States, which said the Egyptian diplomat had failed to reform the U.N. bureaucracy.
Boutros-Ghali was replaced by Ghana's Kofi Annan on Tuesday.
Mandela stunned Taiwan on November 27 by announcing that Pretoria would sever diplomatic ties with Taipei in 1997 in order to recognise Beijing.
South Africa has been the largest of Taiwan's shrinking band of diplomatic partners since longtime Cold War ally South Korea's similar switch in 1992.
Beijing wrested the United Nations' sole China seat away from Taipei in 1971.

China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and has intensified a diplomatic embargo since mid-1995, seeking to prevent what Beijing fears is the island's drift towards independence.
